about.cells: Denmark is divided into {{ cell }} m cells.
about.cellsDetail: Denmark is divided into {{ cell }} m cells, and into {{ detail }} m cells for the map zoomed in.
about.scores: Every cell gets a value for each data layer, and every block in your weighting turns those values into a score. The map shows the blocks averaged by their importance.
about.homes: Homes are approximated by address points from OpenStreetMap, which are imported from the national address register. Cells in industrial areas are left out.
about.noise: Noise comes from Miljøstyrelsen's 2022 noise mapping where it exists: every road in Copenhagen, Aarhus, Odense and Aalborg, the major roads and railways elsewhere, Copenhagen Airport, and industry in the four cities. A cell has the loudest of them. Other places are estimated from road type and distance.
about.rules: Forests and lakes count from 5 ha. Schools are folkeskoler, friskoler and private schools. Wind turbines are those in operation; their distance is also given in each turbine's total height, of which Danish rules keep 4 from a neighbour. Tax and burglaries are per municipality, and the air per square kilometre.
about.travel: Travel times to your places by car, by bike and on foot are found on OpenStreetMap's roads, paths and ferries, once the server has built its road network; each place says which. By train, and until then, they are estimated from the straight-line distance.
about.colours: Colours are stretched over the points currently shown, so the map always shows the differences that matter. Outside Denmark the map shows Natural Earth's world map.
about.sourcesIntro: Every source the map uses: what it gives, its licence, and how it asks to be credited.
